anchors.summary: Built the per-layout anchor lookup for PickPlaceCounterToSink by instantiating all 50 pretrain layouts (11..60) with zeroed spawn deviations; all 50 succeeded, zero failures. Output JSON pool_layout_anchors.json maps layout id -> {base: [x,y], base_yaw: yaw_rad, base_ori_raw: [euler xyz], sink: [x,y], sink_z}. init_robot_base_ori turned out to be an euler-xyz triple, so base_yaw is its z component (values are multiples of pi/2: 0, 1.571, 3.142, 4.712/-1.571). Minimum pairwise distance between base anchors: 0.0148 m, between layouts 20 and 36. Ten closest pairs: 20-36 0.0148, 13-44 0.0228, 23-45 0.0230, 21-27 0.0320, 11-36 0.0511, 32-39 0.0544, 14-30 0.0584, 11-20 0.0659, 23-41 0.0840, 28-32 0.0963 m. Ambiguity analysis vs demo spawn jitter (+-0.15 m x, +-0.05 m y): using the worst-case overlap box (dx<0.30, dy<0.10) there are 31 layout pairs whose jittered base positions can collide; 2 are resolved by yaw (14-30, 16-43), 1 by absolute sink position (16-37), leaving 28 pairs ambiguous from base pose alone. Sink position adds almost no independent signal because in every layout the sink center sits exactly 0.5 m in front of the base anchor along the facing direction (dsink is approximately equal to dbase for all ambiguous pairs). Conclusion: nearest-anchor lookup identifies most layouts, but with min anchor separation 0.0148 m being far below the jitter magnitude (~0.158 m worst case), base-position nearest-anchor cannot uniquely identify the layout for those 28 overlapping pairs; a disambiguating feature independent of base pose (e.g. counter/fixture geometry or camera content) would be needed for them.
anchors.caveats: 1) base_yaw is taken directly from init_robot_base_ori's euler-z component and is left unwrapped (e.g. 4.712 rather than -1.571); wrap to [-pi, pi) before comparing yaws. base_ori_raw is preserved in the JSON for reference. 2) Anchors were extracted with style id fixed at 11 and seed 0; base anchor and sink position are determined by layout geometry so style should not matter, but this was not verified across styles. 3) The ambiguity count (28 unresolved pairs) assumes worst-case uniform jitter of +-0.15 m x / +-0.05 m y in the layout frame; if actual demos jitter less, fewer pairs are practically confusable. 4) sink pos is the fixture center from env.get_fixture('sink').pos; sink_z (~0.958 m) is included as a separate key. 5) The JSON keys are strings '11'..'60' as requested.

feats.summary: Extracted per-demo features for all 9,885 pool episodes and all 108 sample episodes into pool_features.json ({"pool": [...], "sample": [...]}, floats rounded to 3 decimals). Grasp detection: 9,885/9,885 pool and 108/108 sample episodes got a valid grasp frame (zero nulls). Grasp rule used: gripper action dim is action[11] (modality.json "gripper_close", slice 11:12), values exactly {-1,+1} with -1=open, +1=close (verified: gripper_qpos ~0.041 open drops to ~0.025-0.027 after the +1 transition); grasp_frame = first frame where action[11] flips to +1 and remains +1 for >=10 consecutive frames. Quat convention: base_rotation state[3:7] is XYZW (scalar-last) — validated on the sample against ep_meta init_robot_base_ori yaw: max yaw error 2.5e-7 rad for xyzw vs pi off for wxyz; quat x,y components are exactly 0 in every episode (pure yaw), so full-quat rotation and yaw-only Rz are identical. EEF frame convention: end_effector_position_relative is in the base-LOCAL frame — frame-0 rel is nearly constant ([0.247,-0.006,0.595], std<0.012) across episodes spanning all 5 base yaws {-pi,-pi/2,0,pi/2,pi}, which would be impossible if it were world-frame offsets; therefore world_eef_xy = base_xy + Rz(byaw) @ rel_xy (computed at the grasp frame). Physical sanity: grasp world z = 0.7 (state base z) + 0.263 (mean rel z at close) ~= 0.96 m ~= counter height. CRITICAL VALIDATION passed: sample frame-0 base_position xy vs ep_meta init_robot_base_pos max |diff| = 1e-6 m (note: state base z=0.7 constant vs ep_meta z=0 — a fixed base-link height offset; xy is what matches). Sample rows carry gt_layout, gt_style, gt_cat (from object_cfgs entry name=="obj" -> info.cat; present for all 108). Pool has 79 distinct cat_name values (top: cucumber 269, corn 241, rolling pin 240); pool grasp_frame median 100 (range 53-200); grasp xy ranges gx [-0.606, 6.691], gy [-4.995, -0.222].
feats.caveats: Sample episodes.jsonl has no trajectory_id, so "traj" is null for all sample rows. cat_name is the natural-language name parsed from tasks[0] (e.g. "rolling pin") while gt_cat is the RoboCasa category slug (e.g. "sweet_potato") — spacing/underscore normalization needed if joining them. base_position z in the state stream is 0.70 (base-link height), not the 0.0 stored in ep_meta; only xy was validated/used. World-EEF rotation was validated indirectly (home-pose invariance across yaws + counter-height z check), since ep_meta stores no absolute EEF or fixture world positions.

asm.summary:
Wrote fx_pool.json (0.57 MB): recovered factor table for all 9,885 MG pool demos, fields [i,cat,h,w,layout,r,x,y,side,ambig,len], cats array reused verbatim from fx_episodes.json (indexes align), 36 arm lists (12 arms*.json files x core/random/base, verified identical to sources; 2,568 distinct pool demos selected by >=1 arm).

KEY DIAGNOSIS (both prescribed validation gates tripped, root cause found): eval obj_x/y_rel = obj_abs - init_robot_base_pos in WORLD axes with the per-episode JITTERED base (found in policy_analysis/rollout_eval.py:_target_object_xy). So (a) the planned per-layout affine abs->rel fit can never be near-exact — all 100 axis fits had R2 0.21-0.99, residual = base jitter, confirmed by showing implied base = abs-rel always lands in a rotated jitter box (+-0.05 toward-counter, +-0.15 along-counter; 0/7112 outside a padded 0.055/0.20 box) around the zero-jitter anchors; placement was therefore computed DIRECTLY as (gx-bx, gy-by), which is exact by construction and layout-independent. (b) Naive nearest-anchor gave only 84.6% on unambiguous sample rows because same-wall layouts sit closer than the +-0.15 lateral jitter (20/36: 0.015 m, 13/44 and 23/45: 0.023 m); replaced with yaw-matched rotated-jitter-box assignment: SAMPLE accuracy = 100% on unambiguous rows (66/66), 75.9% overall, and the gt layout is in the strict candidate set 108/108 times (mean set size 1.81) — ambiguous rows (34.9% of pool) are honest same-wall confusions between geometrically near-identical layouts, so r/x/y/side/h/w are unaffected by them.

REPORT NUMBERS: layout acc on sample = 0.759 overall / 1.000 unambiguous (n=66); per-layout pool counts mean 197.7, median 198, range 110-284 (uniform ~198/layout as expected; skew confined to confusable same-wall groups, e.g. 20:284 vs 36:110); placement_valid_frac = 1.000, out-of-region (|x| or |y| >1.1) = 0/9885, pool r distribution p5/med/p95 = 0.38/0.55/0.73 vs eval 0.40/0.57/0.76, 100% in [0.2,0.9]; side split +1:5044 / -1:4841; category coverage 79/79 pool categories (kettle->kettle_non_electric alias, 75 demos; normalization certified 108/108 exact gt_cat matches on sample); fx cats h/w match CSV per-category means to <=0.0005. Arm sizes: each core/random 200 (coverage 201, saturate core 610), base 400.
asm.caveats: 1) Layout label is a best-guess for the 34.9% ambig=1 rows (multiple anchors' jitter boxes contain the base); confusions are strictly within same-wall near-identical-geometry groups, and the true layout was always in the candidate set on the validation sample — use ambig=0 rows for per-layout analyses or treat ambiguous labels as group-level. 2) Pool placement uses grasp-frame world EEF xy as proxy for object init position (eval used object body pos at frame 0); r-distribution match with eval suggests the proxy error is small but it is not zero (EEF-vs-object-center offset, pre-grasp nudges). 3) side for the ~3 layouts whose eval episodes covered only one region uses a yaw-based geometric fallback for the axis choice. 4) h/w are per-CATEGORY eval means, not per-instance dims. 5) The prescribed affine-fit path was intentionally replaced after diagnosis (documented in stats.notes and build_fx_pool2.py header); per-layout single-affine R2 ranged 0.21-0.99 and would have injected up to +-0.15 jitter error into x/y had it been used.

verify.reasoning: All four independent checks pass. (1) An independent re-implementation of the yaw-matched rotated-jitter-box assignment on the 108-episode sample reproduces the claimed numbers exactly: 82/108 = 0.7593 overall, 66/66 = 1.000 unambiguous, gt_layout in the candidate set 108/108; all 26 misses are same-wall confusables with gt always in the feasible set; a fully independent nearest-yaw-compatible-anchor baseline gives a consistent 83/108; my assignment matches the stored pool layout column 9885/9885 with ambig_frac 0.3491; gt_cat matches slug(cat_name) 108/108. (2) On 5 random layouts (51,18,12,58,28) assigned pool grasps form two clean clusters flanking the sink at lateral offsets ~-0.55/+0.54 m (aggregate -0.551/+0.540, sd ~0.10, only 0.3% of demos in the |lat|<0.2 gap), matching the eval side analysis' +-0.57 m; the side column is exactly 0-or-1 consistent per layout (world-rel-axis sign convention) and its flip pattern matches the eval convention on all 41 comparable layouts. (3) Per-layout counts: 50 layouts, min 110 / max 284 / mean 197.7 (~198 expected), none <100 or >350; skew is confined to same-wall confusable groups. Category check vs rcless_raw/cand_meta.json: exactly 9,036 overlapping episodes, 500/500 spot-check and 9,036/9,036 full match (with kettle->kettle_non_electric alias). (4) Pool r is unimodal (single peak ~0.5-0.55), median 0.55, p5-p95 0.38-0.73, nearly identical to eval-success r (median 0.55, TV distance 0.028) and closer to eval-successes than eval-all (TV 0.077) — the expected signature of successful MG executions from the same sampler; no bimodality or absurd mass, and no large rim deficit either (pool frac r>0.44 = 0.838 vs 0.856 for eval successes). Caveat (already honestly disclosed in the file's own stats/notes): the layout label is only ~76% accurate for the 35% ambiguous rows, but confusions are near-identical-geometry same-wall layouts flagged by the ambig column, and the r/x/y/side/h/w factors are unaffected, as the cluster and distribution checks confirm.
verify.corrected: No corrections needed. Verified figures: sample layout accuracy 0.7593 (1.000 unambiguous, n=66; gt in candidate set 108/108); pool ambig_frac 0.3491; 50 layouts with counts 110-284 (mean 197.7); categories 9036/9036 match vs cand_meta; sink-flank clusters at -0.551/+0.540 m lateral; pool r median 0.55, TV distance to eval-success r = 0.028.
